input.body:
label: bug
file: src/components/ExportButton.tsx

The `handleClick` handler in `ExportButton` only attaches a `.then()` to the `exportReport` promise and never a `.catch()`. When the export request fails (e.g. a non-2xx response causes `exportReport` to throw), `setBusy(false)` is never called, so the button stays stuck in the disabled "busy" state until the page is reloaded. The fix should catch the rejection, reset `busy` to `false`, and surface an error toast to the user.

input.title: Reset export button state after a failed export
input.body: File: src/components/ExportButton.tsx. In handleClick, the call to exportReport only has a .then() handler that clears busy and shows a success toast; if the returned promise rejects (e.g. a non-2xx response throws in exportReport), setBusy(false) is never called, so the button stays disabled until the page is reloaded. Add a .catch() (or use try/catch with async/await) that resets busy to false and shows an error toast when the export fails.
